03 / THE SCIENCE

What comes next
starts with what changed.

The model learns the difference between a main shock and its aftershock: when it occurs, where it happens, how deep it is, and its recorded class.

Explore the model ↗
RESEARCH PROJECT · NOT AN EARLY WARNING SYSTEM
01

Start with the main shock.

Time, coordinates, depth and class become the starting point. Seasonal and geographic features add context.

02

Learn the differences.

A median baseline, LightGBM and Random Forest estimate changes in five targets. A blend is evaluated too.

03

Let validation decide.

Nine-fold cross-validation compares mean absolute error for each target, then selects the best candidate.

04

Reconstruct the aftershock.

Predicted changes are added to the main shock to estimate the aftershock. The interactive form runs the fitted model, with validation errors shown above.
